cases.evidence: Emitted a pronoun/tense before the verb and destination arrived; translator invented 'it will come'.
cases.proposed_rule: Do not mark a cut that would emit a definite or co‑referring NP (e.g. 'the X' / pronoun) before the main verb or its complements (destination/PP) appear.

example_pair.input: ship, the ship was on its way to X
example_pair.output: ship, the ship was on its way to X <SEG:1>

cases.evidence: Translated modifiers ('weekly') before the head noun, producing nonsense ('weekly magazine').
cases.proposed_rule: Never cut between stacked modifiers and their head noun; if tokens like 'weekly','regular','structured' precede a nearby noun, delay the boundary until that noun appears.

cases.evidence: Cut after reporting verb allowed a mistranslation of entity type/number ('militant' → group).
cases.proposed_rule: Lower confidence for boundaries immediately after reporting verbs (said/suspect/believe/report) when followed within 1–4 tokens by an article ('a/an/the') or a parenthetical '(', since entity type/qualifier follows.

example_pair.input: they suspect an alleged Daesh (ISIL) militant
example_pair.output: they suspect an alleged Daesh (ISIL) militant <SEG:1>

cases.evidence: Rendered 'for others' as carrying people rather than others' luggage (wrong participant).
cases.proposed_rule: Do not cut immediately after 'for' when the phrase is 'for X' (e.g. 'for others'); delay until the noun/possessed item or dash-subclause arrives to disambiguate possession vs beneficiary.

example_pair.input: Carrying for others - Never let your bags
example_pair.output: Carrying for others - Never let your bags <SEG:1>

cases.evidence: Committed to a transfer/compromise verb meaning before seeing its object ('to some economic demands'), yielding wrong verb choice.
cases.proposed_rule: Avoid cutting immediately after verbs of transfer/compromise (give, give way, give in, hand over) when a 'to' prepositional object or its NP is pending; wait for the 'to' phrase.

example_pair.input: he did give way to some demands
example_pair.output: he did give way to some demands <SEG:1>

cases.evidence: Auxiliary + passive separated from participle; passive voice/argument structure lost and translation degraded.
cases.proposed_rule: Do not mark a boundary between a copula/auxiliary (is/was/are) and a following past participle (V‑ed); keep auxiliary+participle together until the verb phrase is complete.

example_pair.input: air travel is only rarely booked
example_pair.output: air travel is only rarely booked <SEG:1>

cases.evidence: Split the verb phrase from its object ('the national sovereignty'), causing loss of the object and mistranslation.
cases.proposed_rule: Do not cut between verbs like 'seek(s)/sought to' and their following noun‑phrase object; wait for the object NP ('the ...') to appear before emitting the verb phrase.

summary: The prompt still allows early cuts that force the translator to guess a missing head, object, or participant, producing pronouns, wrong noun types, or incorrect voice. Two levers will help: (1) placement rules that forbid cuts that separate auxiliaries/verbs/modifiers from their immediate heads/objects, and (2) a priority rule that demotes cuts after reporting verbs when an article or parenthetical qualifier follows. Together these reduce risky top‑rank picks without banning all comma cuts.

aggregate.dominant_basis: No corpus rate identifies a dominant failure. Read the cases and `judge_distribution` for WHICH mechanism to fix — do not infer a rate from `case_label_counts`, those cases were selected for being the worst.

coverage.of: all sentences scored — a true corpus rate
coverage.meaning: sentences where the tightest budget asked for boundaries the prompt never marked, so pieces are missing outright

premature_among_judged.of: boundaries judged this iteration, selected as the WORST by measured contradiction — NOT a corpus rate, do not compare it against `coverage`

case_label_counts.of: the selected worst cases — NOT a rate
